key_insight: Benchmark design can dramatically change how well LLMs appear to perform on medical exams, revealing that MCQA scores may overstate true clinical competence.
clinical_relevance: For medical AI evaluation, harder and less bias-prone exam formats may be needed before trusting model performance as evidence of real-world reasoning ability.
method: Expanded Polish medical exam benchmark with 15,000+ added questions
Added two new domains and four structural changes to reduce MCQA-specific artifacts
Evaluated 21 LLMs across English and Polish exams
evidence_signal: The best model (Qwen3.5-122B) fell by 28.4 points on English and 31 points on Polish exams under the harder setup, with low evidence of data contamination.
watch_item: Strong multiple-choice performance may still reflect guessing or answer-pattern bias, so benchmark scores should not be treated as direct proof of clinical competence.
paper_title: Reassessing High-Performing LLMs on Polish Medical Exams: True Competence or Bias-Driven Performance?
